name: Fantasy Code RPG
inspiration: 1990s Japanese 16-bit RPGs (late SNES era). Feel, never copied assets.
lighting: top-left key light, 2-4 shades per surface, coloured outlines

cast.rule: All characters are adults. Heroines get glamorous 90s JRPG styling; never explicit.

ui.window: Code-green vertical gradient #0e3a22 > #06200f > #020a06 with faint scanlines, 3 px pale border #c8ffd4, inner 3 px #1f8a3c line, outer ink line, soft glow. Classic blue is a setting.
ui.background: Digital-rain overlay (assets/brand/rain.png, generated by rain.cjs) behind every scene

voice: Plain words on screen; technical detail one click away. Classic JRPG names for real states.
originality: No copied sprites, music, logos, window skins or characters from existing games.
vibe: Matrix meets fantasy: green code rains behind every scene; swords and dragons live inside it. Designed like a 1990s Japanese RPG studio would.

bestiary.rule: Every monster comes from real folklore and its legend matches a real problem; defeating it means doing the real fix.

monsters.hydra: a bug that keeps coming back: fix it and add a test
monsters.nurikabe: something blocking the work: find the root cause
monsters.will-o-the-wisp: a problem that only happens sometimes: reproduce it first
monsters.kitsune: a bug disguised as a different bug
monsters.chimera: one request that is really three: split it
monsters.phoenix: something that keeps crashing and restarting
monsters.sphinx: nobody said exactly what is wanted: only you can answer
monsters.book-mimic: instructions that are out of date

bestiary.adaptive: Monsters adapt to how you play; skipped tests grow Hydra heads; regional variants; no final boss.

logo: FANTASY CODE in gold bevel, RPG in silver, sword behind. No tagline.
